rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline that covers the main risks. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 8 mm apart across x = -0.016 to +0.016 m, so the line (25 mm wide) always covers at least one or two sensors. They sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the bend. Sensor size 0.012 m is smaller than the tape, which keeps the readings sensitive to small offsets. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give moderate yaw authority without excessive wheel speed. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor. Mass 0.8 kg is mid-range. Controller: sensor weights are antisymmetric (-1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), so a line to the left gives a positive signal and steers left. kp = 3.0 is a moderate proportional gain, kd = 0.15 damps overshoot on the curves, and ki = 0.05 is small to avoid integral windup. base_speed = 1.6 is a fast but not saturating demand, chosen to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed for the 3 s limit. line_loss = last_direction recovers toward the side the line was last seen. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. Hypotheses to check: (1) the speed target is reachable without going off track; (2) kp is high enough to track the tighter bends; (3) line-loss events are rare. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, RMS and max error, line-loss count, and steering oscillation, which together show whether the next revision should raise speed, adjust kp/kd, or widen the sensor spread.
